decisions.reason: As a close-to-core turnaround product with its own market-facing presence, it remains a low-cost strategic option that fits the firm's integrated airport-operations direction and shows no clear reason for abandonment yet.
This connectivity module still leverages the firm's installed base and systems-integration strengths, so the option value of keeping it available remains higher than the likely cost of continuation.

Revenue and billing software is somewhat less central to the firm's core operational stack, so it faces the highest pruning risk, but it still supports the broader digital platform and is worth retaining while demand becomes clearer.
Equipment monitoring software aligns closely with the firm's engineering, maintenance, and lifecycle-service capabilities, making continued market presence the more sensible choice.
This apron resource management module is near the firm's core offer and supports end-to-end automation, so keeping the option open remains attractive.

The controller safety alert service is strategically well aligned with the firm's safety and tower positioning, and despite potentially long validation cycles it still merits another year of retention.
